title: Concrete core strength
intro:
Eight cores were drilled from a bridge deck and crushed. Their compressive strengths had a mean of **31.6 MPa** and a standard deviation of **2.4 MPa**. The population standard deviation is not known.

Build the **95 %** confidence interval for the mean strength of the deck: find the standard error, the critical value, the margin of error, and the two limits. Give every answer to two decimals or more (three for the critical value).

StandardError.says: That is s, the spread of single cores. The standard error of the mean is s/√n.
You divided by n = 8. The standard error divides by √n = √8.

Critical.says: That is z. σ is unknown and estimated by s from only eight cores, so use t with n − 1 = 7 degrees of freedom.
That is t with 8 degrees of freedom. The degrees of freedom are n − 1 = 7.
That is t_{0.05, 7}, with all of α in one tail. A two-sided 95 % interval puts 0.025 in each tail: t_{0.025, 7}.

MarginOfError.says: You used z = 1.960. With s from eight cores, use t_{0.025, 7}.
You multiplied the critical value by s. Multiply it by the standard error s/√n.
You used t with 8 degrees of freedom. Use n − 1 = 7.

Lower.says: You used z = 1.960. With s from eight cores, use t_{0.025, 7}.
You subtracted t × s. Subtract t × s/√n.

Upper.says: You used z = 1.960. With s from eight cores, use t_{0.025, 7}.
You added t × s. Add t × s/√n.

hints: σ is unknown, so this is a t interval: x̄ ± t_{0.025, n−1} × s/√n.
Standard error = 2.4 / √8. Degrees of freedom = 8 − 1 = 7; t_{0.025, 7} is in a t table, or stats.t.ppf(0.975, 7), or qt(0.975, 7).
Margin of error = t × standard error. Lower = 31.6 − margin, upper = 31.6 + margin.
